### 2026-10-12 – # Started Modelling

**2.8h**

# Started Modelling

Started using Fusion 360 to model reference parts.

The Stepper motor was somewhat annoying to do, as there were conflicting datasheets as to the shaft length, but eventually after spending too much time looking, I found the exact datasheet of the one I am planning to buy.

![stepper motor image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/a4c2e424d67058f03cbf2db473e8b4824146053d33c5bfbeb2cbed7b46c87579.png)
![stepper motor 3d model](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/803f41e9033cc2e0d20859237aaa2f882e0b842e747d8ed00e9e7f6991d01aa8.png)

## Started the layout

In my mind, the layout of a 3D model is always the most important part. And to this end, every time I model reference parts, then go through a bunch of options orienting them. Usually I do this a lot more with parameters and configurations, but as I'm on a tighter time deadline for this project, I only went through a few layouts before I ended up with one I was happy with.

![part layouts](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/843ac2e5d430bbda7836e9d90ef63a066d53b28f19cdeb7e00eed459d711768f.png)

So my plan is to have the stepper at the top, then try to balance it out with the batteries on the other side, and further towards the bottom

## Other notes

Also had to change the PCB design, as I realised that with how I'm planning to drive the curtain cord, the motor current might become a problem, so I added in a current sensor - or to be more specific, I removed my voltage divider and battery level sensing for an I2C module that does both.

## Next Steps

I think it will be more a problem of deciding when to stop. As for 3D modelling, I've mastered Fusion to the extent that I will always be able to improve designs, but in this case, I think simulations are likely redundant.

But anyway:
- Planning to add a bearing for shear support for the motor.
- And wondering whether to have the PCB as slide in or screw in.
- Also whether to use a 2S battery holder, or try and integrate my own, and just form the connections by bending some copper strips.

Example:
![Example of a custom 18650 holder](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8586e4572c21fbbe1a35e77979155a392f71758d16661b1f9d4262954f14901c.png)

Maybe not as botched as this, but I think in the style of standard nickel tabs, but just copper tabs bend around some 3D printed brackets?
